constraints: tree-sitter-php crate version must be >= 7 days old per cargo deny package age check; version 0.25.2 is current and meets this requirement
PHP grammar uses tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE (not LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY) to support .php files with embedded HTML; queries must match only PHP node kinds
extract_inheritance must handle base_clause and class_interface_clause as child nodes (not fields) since PHP grammar does not expose parent_class/base_classes/interfaces fields
DEFUSE_QUERY must capture variable_name nodes (not bare identifiers) because PHP uses variable_name wrapper node type
No extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver, find_receiver_type handlers required (marked as 'no consumer since #1807')
Integration test must cover HTML-template edge case (mixed PHP and HTML) to verify zero ERROR nodes
test_coverage: Existing test coverage for language registration: crates/aptu-coder-core/src/languages/mod.rs has test_get_language_info_known, test_get_language_info_unknown, and test_language_info_query_fields_consistency. Each language module (java.rs, swift.rs, python.rs) has unit tests for ELEMENT_QUERY compilation and matching, inheritance extraction, and DEFUSE_QUERY write/read sites. Integration tests in crates/aptu-coder/tests/integration_tests.rs use call_tool_raw to invoke analyze_directory, analyze_file, analyze_module with real files and verify language field, element counts, and call/import extraction.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Direct Port from Issue #1861 Implementation Notes
approaches.description: Use the exact ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY, and inheritance extraction logic documented in the closed issue #1861. This approach leverages pre-validated node kinds and field names from the grammar, minimizing discovery work.
pros: Implementation notes already validated against tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 grammar
Code examples provided in issue reduce query development time
Inheritance extraction pattern (base_clause and class_interface_clause as child nodes) already documented
cons: Less opportunity for independent verification of grammar node kinds
Relies on external issue documentation rather than first-principles grammar inspection

approaches.name: Approach 2: Grammar-First Discovery with Minimal Queries
approaches.description: Parse sample PHP files (function, class with extends/implements, interface, trait, enum) with tree-sitter-php, inspect the AST to discover node kinds and field names, then write queries from scratch. Start with ELEMENT_QUERY and CALL_QUERY only, defer REFERENCE_QUERY and DEFUSE_QUERY to a second pass.
pros: Deep understanding of PHP grammar structure
Ability to optimize queries for PHP-specific idioms
Validates grammar against actual parsing output
cons: Requires manual AST inspection and query testing
Risk of missing node kinds or field names if sample files are incomplete

approaches.name: Approach 3: Hybrid - Verify Issue #1861 Queries Against Grammar, Then Implement
approaches.description: Cross-reference the issue #1861 implementation notes against the official tree-sitter-php grammar (php/src/node-types.json and define-grammar.js), verify each node kind and field name, then implement with confidence. This combines the speed of Approach 1 with the rigor of Approach 2.
pros: Catches any grammar changes between issue writing and implementation
Produces well-documented code with inline grammar citations
cons: Requires access to both issue documentation and grammar source
Slightly longer than pure port but justified by verification

recommendation: Approach 3 (Hybrid - Verify and Implement). The issue #1861 implementation notes are comprehensive and pre-validated, but cross-referencing against the official grammar (which Context7 confirms exists at v0.25.2) ensures correctness and documents the source. This approach takes ~1-2 hours and produces the highest-quality implementation: verified queries, proper inheritance extraction, and test coverage. The five files touched (php.rs, mod.rs, lang.rs, Cargo.toml root, README.md) are all straightforward registry and query additions with no architectural changes.

pub struct LanguageInfo {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub language: Language,
    pub element_query: &'static str,
    pub call_query: &'static str,
    pub reference_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub import_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_trait_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub defuse_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub extract_function_name: Option<ExtractFunctionNameHandler>,
    pub find_method_for_receiver: Option<FindMethodForReceiverHandler>,
    pub find_receiver_type: Option<FindReceiverTypeHandler>,
    pub extract_inheritance: Option<ExtractInheritanceHandler>,
}
element_query_draft:
r"
(function_definition
  name: (name) @function_name) @function
(method_declaration
  name: (name) @method_name) @function
(class_declaration
  name: (name) @class_name) @class
(interface_declaration
  name: (name) @interface_name) @class
(trait_declaration
  name: (name) @trait_name) @class
(enum_declaration
  name: (name) @enum_name) @class
"
inheritance_walk_citation: For a class_declaration node in tree-sitter-php, walk the child nodes (not fields, since base_clause and class_interface_clause are not named fields in class_declaration per node-types.json). Iterate through all children: when a child.kind() == 'base_clause' is found, iterate its named_children to extract each name node and format as 'extends ClassName'; when a child.kind() == 'class_interface_clause' is found, iterate its named_children to extract each name node and format as 'implements InterfaceName'. The same pattern applies to interface_declaration (which may have interface_base_clause for extends) and enum_declaration (which may have class_interface_clause for implements). Source: github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php blob master common/define-grammar.js base_clause and class_interface_clause rules, and php/src/node-types.json class_declaration, interface_declaration, trait_declaration, enum_declaration entries.
